description: Guards the basic happy path: a small web shop yields a schema-valid estimate that mentions the domain and stays in a plausible size band.
turns: We are a small independent bookstore and we want an online shop. Customers should browse a catalog of books, search by title or author, add books to a cart and pay by card. We would like to build it with Django and Stripe, and the owner needs a simple admin page to manage stock and orders.

description: Guards a mobile domain: the estimate mentions the workout domain and the requested mobile stack.
turns: We want a mobile app for iOS and Android where people log their workouts, follow weekly training plans and see progress charts. Users sign in with an email account, and the app should sync workouts to a backend so nothing is lost when someone changes phones. We are thinking about React Native.

description: Guards a data-engineering domain: a nightly pipeline estimate that mentions data work and the named tools.
turns: Every night we need to collect sales exports from three regional shops, clean and merge them, load the result into a warehouse and refresh a reporting dashboard for the finance team. We want it orchestrated with Airflow, transformed with Python and loaded into PostgreSQL, with alerts when a nightly run fails.

description: Guards an internal-tool domain: a small approval workflow still produces a full estimate with the domain vocabulary.
turns: Our company needs a small internal tool where employees request time off, their manager approves or rejects the request, and the human resources team sees a calendar of who is away. It should send an email when a request changes state and only be reachable from our company network.

description: Guards the audience heuristic: business vocabulary (CEO, board, investors, ROI) must resolve to the executive tier and that tier must be reported back.
turns: Our CEO and the board want a customer loyalty program for our coffee shop chain. The investors expect a clear ROI within the first year, so please estimate how much building a loyalty app with points and rewards would cost and how long it would take.

description: Guards the audience heuristic: delivery vocabulary (sprint, backlog, roadmap, milestone, stakeholders) with no executive cue must resolve to the pm tier.
turns: We run two-week sprints and our product backlog for a customer support portal keeps growing. Please estimate the portal so we can fit it into the roadmap with three milestones and share the plan with our stakeholders. Customers open tickets, track their status and rate the answer.

description: Guards the audience heuristic: technical vocabulary (API, endpoint, microservice, schema) with no executive or pm cue must resolve to the developer tier.
turns: We need a new inventory microservice that exposes a REST API with endpoints to create, update and list products and stock levels. It needs a clear database schema, input validation and automated tests, and it must be easy to call from our existing order system.

turns: Please estimate a small internal reporting API with a couple of endpoints that read sales numbers from our database and return them as JSON for the finance team, plus a basic access token check.

Add a customer reviews feature so that readers can rate books and write short reviews on every book page.

description: Guards conversation memory on a data project: follow-up requirements are merged into one growing estimate for the same project.

Also add a Slack notification that tells the finance team when the pipeline fails or when an anomaly is found.

Also add push notifications that warn a driver when a new urgent parcel is assigned to them.
